extracted.intended_audience: readers of Popular Science Monthly (educated general public, scientists, and engineers)
extracted.subtask_description: Magazine-style reviews and editorial commentary evaluating books, inventions, and technical research for a general-scientific readership; includes both literary criticism and technical assessment (e.g., storage batteries, scientific treatises, archaeological works).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial viability of a storage-battery
rubrics_metrics.description: In order for the storage-battery to take its place as an important element in the growing industrial applications of electricity, it must reach a considerably higher efficiency than it appears to have yet attained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiments (Conservatoire des Arts-et-Metiers) measured: (1) the mechanical labor expended in charging the battery; (2) the quantity of electricity stored during the charge; (3) the quantity of electricity given out during the discharge; and (4) the electrical work actually effected during the discharge. On this showing the battery returned forty per cent of the total mechanical power spent in charging it, and sixty per cent of the electrical work spent upon it. The mechanical-return figure includes dynamo efficiency and so is not solely the battery's performance. These results indicate the battery 'does not seem to have reached a commercial stage' though continued attention may make this change in the near future.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability of applications for storage-batteries
rubrics_metrics.description: A thoroughly commercial storage-battery has a wide field of usefulness: notably as an element in a system of electric distribution for both light and power; in isolated electric plants for suburban and country houses; and in propulsion of cars on street and suburban railways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific benefits: with a battery in each house a smaller producing plant in continuous operation can replace a larger one, and groups of battery-cells can be connected so arc and incandescent lamps and machinery run independently. Batteries are well adapted where wind and water power can be used for charging. For railway propulsion they could displace steam where there are good water-power facilities at sufficiently frequent intervals, or proximity to coal-mines to generate charging electricity at the pit; key advantage is avoiding fire, steam, and smoke of locomotives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic criterion for continuing serial publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions to continue a serial publication should be guided by financial returns versus costs: payments to compilers, printing, and other expenses must be weighed against sales income; if returns do not promise to repay expenses or yield a reasonable interest, discontinuance is justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: over fourteen years payments and printing costs amounted to large sums while returns (including foreign) were small, leaving a substantial deficit. Even with appreciation of work, continuation is untenable when post-publication returns beyond initial small sales do not repay sunk capital or provide satisfactory interest. Consider also public appreciation and potential future demand; acceptances of external funds should be applied as a public trust, not for private benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria for a valuable scientific monograph
rubrics_metrics.description: A good scientific monograph should be 'from both a scientific and a practical point of view ... among the most interesting and valuable'—it should present an able statement of the latest knowledge and have practical import.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reviewer praises works that: make the author's stand-point clear; treat the subject (e.g., memory) as a biological fact with study of nervous structures, properties, and activities; identify fundamental components of the phenomenon; provide more trustworthy knowledge than preceding treatises; and yield results that are 'highly practical' for correcting erroneous views. Clarity of conception and up-to-date synthesis of evidence are important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for evaluating works on religious criticism / theological inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Books addressing the conflict between theology and liberty of thought are valuable insofar as they raise fundamental questions (e.g., liberty of thought) and provide informed, independent scholarship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such works should: clearly present the nature and historic/contemporary dimensions of the conflict; engage systematically with traditional theology from the point of view of modern criticism; contain chapters 'full of information' that serve as an 'excellent introduction' for readers wanting to understand the current state of liberal inquiry in theology; and show honest, fearless research even if it invites repression of thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for an archaeological/monument publication
rubrics_metrics.description: A high-quality work on monuments (e.g., Egyptian obelisks) should combine narrative of personal adventure and professional achievement with an exhaustive historical and archaeological account and scientific study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect detailed descriptions of methods used in transportation and erection, translations of inscriptions, records and photographs of monuments, notes on ancient quarrying/transport methods, scientific analyses of materials (e.g., polariscopic sections), and plentiful illustrations. Production values (good illustrations, thorough documentation) and leaving 'nothing wanting' are signs of excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for an experimental/theoretical physics treatise
rubrics_metrics.description: A robust treatise in hydrodynamics/acoustics should address the correct order of inquiry (study production mechanisms before secondary equilibrating factors) and combine speculative development with careful application to natural phenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper procedure example: determine how waves are produced on water by wind first, then investigate gravity's role in restoring equilibrium—avoid assuming the wave's existence and begging the question. Useful structure includes speculative chapters to clarify concepts, followed by theory development (e.g., rolling contact, conic resistance, vortices) and application of established principles to explain natural currents and wave formation. Balance speculative discussion with experimental/extended investigations; withhold incomplete sections until further work when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for a readable and instructive biography
rubrics_metrics.description: A good biography should be 'one of the most readable and instructive' and do justice to the character and achievements of its subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reviewer values biographies that vividly bring out character, provide context for the subject's major achievements (e.g., role in public works like canal-building), document contributions to political and social movements (e.g., anti-slavery), present clear narrative and judgment, and make previously fragmentary or obscure histories accessible and informative.
